prompt: What does a test with `httptest.NewRecorder` need besides the handler?
hint: The handler's one method takes two arguments.

choices.text: A free port, and a server already running on it
choices.why: That is `NewServer`. A recorder is called with no network at all.

choices.text: A request, from `httptest.NewRequest`
choices.why: Right: the test calls `ServeHTTP(rec, req)` directly.

choices.text: A goroutine to run the handler in
choices.why: `ServeHTTP` is an ordinary call in the test's own goroutine.

choices.text: An `http.Client` to send the request
choices.why: Nothing is sent; the request value is handed to the method.

prompt: The first `Handler` set `Content-Type` after calling `Encode`. Why did the JSON go out as `text/plain`?

choices.text: `json.Encoder` always writes plain text
choices.why: It writes bytes; the type is a header, and the header was set too late.

choices.text: The recorder cannot carry a `Content-Type`
choices.why: After the fix the same recorder reported `application/json`.

choices.text: Headers go out with the first write
choices.why: Right. With no type set at that moment, `net/http` sniffed one from the body.

choices.text: `http.Error` ran first and fixed the type
choices.why: `http.Error` runs only on the error paths, which passed.

prompt: A test checks the content type with `rec.Header().Get("Content-Type")` instead of `rec.Result()`. Against the first, faulty `Handler`, what would that test report?
hint: `rec.Header()` is the live map the handler writes into.

choices.text: A pass: the live map has the late `Set`
choices.why: Right, which is why the section checks `Result()`: it shows what was actually sent.

choices.text: The same failure that the lesson's own test reported
choices.why: The live map holds `application/json` by the time the handler returns.

choices.text: A compile error
choices.why: `rec.Header()` exists and compiles.

choices.text: A panic inside the recorder
choices.why: Reading a header map does not panic.

prompt: After `ServeHTTP` returns, the response a client would have received comes from the recorder's method ___.

hint: The test log printed its address.

choices.text: Nowhere: it is an object in memory
choices.why: That is the recorder. The server is real and has an address.

choices.text: On port 80 of every interface
choices.why: It takes a free port, and only on the loopback.

choices.text: On a port the test has to choose and pass in
choices.why: It chooses one itself and reports it in `srv.URL`.

choices.text: On a free port of `127.0.0.1`
choices.why: Right: `http://127.0.0.1:40299` in the run quoted.

hint: What does `FSSource` give for a missing file?

choices.text: Because `http.Client` refuses to return 404 responses
choices.why: The client returns any status; `Open` decides what each means.

choices.text: So a missing document means one thing everywhere
choices.why: Right, and `Handler` turns it back into a 404 of its own.

choices.text: Because `fs.ErrNotExist` closes the response body
choices.why: An error value closes nothing; `Open` closes the body itself.

choices.text: To make the 404 count as a test failure
choices.why: The test expects `fs.ErrNotExist` for `b.txt`; it is the success of that check.

prompt: On a 500, `HTTPSource.Open` closes the body before returning its error. Why there and not in `TopOf`?

choices.text: Because `TopOf` closes only files
choices.why: `TopOf` closes any `io.ReadCloser` it is handed.

choices.text: Because the server closes it anyway
choices.why: The body belongs to the client's side and is the client's to close.

choices.text: `TopOf` never sees the body
choices.why: Right. Whoever holds the body last closes it.

choices.text: To make the error message include the body's text
choices.why: The message carries the status, not the body.

prompt: Which of these does a `httptest.NewServer` test exercise that a recorder test does not? Choose all that apply.
hint: One of them is a real connection.

choices.text: The client's request going over a real connection
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A client's deadline cutting a request short
choices.why: Yes, as section 04 showed.

choices.text: The handler's choice of status code
choices.why: A recorder captures that too; it was section 02's subject.

choices.text: The body the handler writes
choices.why: The recorder's `Body` holds it.

choices.text: Thirty seconds
choices.why: There is no default number at all.

choices.text: None
choices.why: Right, so without a deadline it waits as long as the server does.

choices.text: Whatever `GOMAXPROCS` is, in seconds
choices.why: `GOMAXPROCS` has nothing to do with HTTP.

choices.text: The deadline of the test that uses it
choices.why: A client knows nothing about tests.

prompt: In the quoted run, after how many milliseconds did `TestHTTPSourceTimeout` give up?
`TestStuckServer`'s client gave up after 50 ms, yet the test took six seconds. What held it?

choices.text: The context's deadline, which was six seconds
choices.why: The deadline was 50 milliseconds.

choices.text: The race detector, which slows tests down
choices.why: The run had no `-race`.

choices.text: `srv.Close`, waiting for the sleeping handler
choices.why: Right, and it said so: blocked in Close after 5 seconds.

choices.text: `TopOf`, which retried the request
choices.why: `TopOf` makes one call and returns its error.

prompt: A team wants every request from a service to `HTTPSource` limited to two seconds, even when a caller forgets to pass a deadline. Which change does that?
hint: One of the two limits belongs to the client, not to the call.

choices.text: Passing `context.Background()` everywhere
choices.why: `Background` has no deadline at all.

choices.text: A client with `Timeout: 2 * time.Second`
choices.why: Right. It limits every request through that client; a caller's shorter deadline still wins.

choices.text: Making the test handler sleep two seconds
choices.why: That changes the test server, not the service.

choices.text: Using `http.DefaultClient`
choices.why: It has no timeout, which is the problem.

prompt: Put the events of `TestHTTPSourceTimeout` in the order they happen.
hint: The handler is waiting from the moment the request arrives.
items: the 50 ms deadline passes and the client gives up

prompt: Match each thing to test with the tool the lesson uses for it.
hint: Which side of the conversation is under test?

prompt: A colleague replaces `srv.Client()` with `http.DefaultClient` in `TestHTTPSource`. What changes for that test?
hint: What is special about `srv.Client()` for a plain `NewServer`?

choices.text: It fails, because the default client cannot reach `127.0.0.1`
choices.why: Any client reaches the loopback.

choices.text: It hangs, because the default client waits for ever
choices.why: The file server answers at once, so there is nothing to wait for.

choices.text: Nothing visible: for plain HTTP it is an ordinary client
choices.why: Right. The difference shows with `NewTLSServer`, where `srv.Client()` trusts the test certificate.

choices.text: The 404 stops being `fs.ErrNotExist`
choices.why: That mapping is in `HTTPSource.Open`, whatever client it uses.
